newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids were scattered early Monday at $66.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $68.00, with a few at $69.00, feedlot sources said.
Sales were not expected to occur until Wednesday or Thursday because packers reportedly had adequate live inventories following last week's active trading, they said.
Showlists were estimated smaller than last week's in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and unchanged to slightly larger in Kansas, sources in those areas said.
Some cattle on Kansas showlists were carried over from last week, which should result in a slightly larger list, sources there said.
Sales this week were seen at $67.00, unchanged from last week, but prices could move higher if beef prices turn higher, sources said. Beef movement on Friday was strong but at lower prices.
Beef prices on Friday were quoted down $0.03 to $0.40 per cwt, with 269 fabricated loads sold. The sales were reported on the heels of brisk sales Thursday, reported by USDA at 315 loads.
Light support also was expected from firm prices in Nebraska late last week, where a top of $68.50 paid on Friday.
